proposals.evidence: DEDR3296 gives Kannada tuṭi/toḍi, Tulu duḍi and Kota tuc lip. The survey dental/retroflex and voicing variants are preserved; Badaga/Sholaga and Alu Kurumba are comparative lect extensions, and Kota tus is compared with the specifically attested Kota tuc. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR4616 explicitly gives Tamil makaḷ daughter, Malayalam mōḷ, Kota mōḷ, Kannada magaḷ, Tulu magaḷu, Parji māl and Gadaba māl. The selected survey makaḷ/magaḷ and shortened maka/maga/maha forms are comparative daughter extensions, with southern k/g/h variation and loss of final lateral; Parji/Gadaba māl/malu/melu preserve the separately documented central-Dravidian shape. Source gender/sense and vowel notation are retained; compounds and opaque contractions remain unassigned. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR2196 gives Irula kōḍa small monkey, Kota kōṛṇ small monkey, Kodagu kōḍë and Kannada kōḍaga monkey/ape. Selected koḍa/koḍɛ-type survey responses match the southern family; Kota kodunu retains its cluster with epenthetic vowels as a comparative variant. Keep the generic monkey elicitation sense distinct from dictionary species qualifications. proposals.evidence: DEDR4753 gives Tamil maḻai, Malayalam maḻa, Kannada maḻe, Kodagu/Tulu maḷe, Kota may and Toda maw rain. These selected southern survey forms preserve lect-specific lateral, glide, velar or sibilant reflexes and contractions of the rain stem. Minority-lect assignments are comparative extensions; ambiguous source fragments and Indo-Aryan-looking varṣa forms are excluded. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR3491 gives Kannada doḍḍa big and doḍḍitu/doḍḍittu that which is large, Tamil toṭṭa big and Kota doḍ big/great. These survey doḍḍ-/toṭṭ- adjectives and ordinary neuter forms belong with that family; source voicing, gemination and final-vowel differences are retained. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.
